doctrine: AI design workflow combining Claude, Codeex, Claude Design, Figma MCP, and Google Stitch. Token efficiency critical: Codeex uses 3-4x fewer tokens than Claude but produces less polished designs. Claude produces highest quality designs and code. Google Stitch for fast, low-token early-stage iteration. Training AI on design systems requires sequential prompts on variables, text styles, and components (form elements, navigation, data display). Design-to-code pipeline: Figma → Claude Code → Figma (edits) → Codeex (refinement) → Figma (polish) → Claude (production code). Bidirectional Figma MCP enables code-to-Figma conversion. Components + constraints solve responsive design. Styles (colors, text) enforce consistency across instances. Auto layout manages spacing and alignment. Always provide design system file and Figma MCP access when prompting. Use design tokens (3-tier: brand/alias/mapped) for scale. Building iOS apps: Figma mockups → Windsurf/Cursor (React Native/Expo) → iOS Simulator → TestFlight → App Store. Mobile design requires single feature MVP, onboarding, proper user flows before development. Setup Figma MCP + Figma skills before coding. Push designs to Figma first for visual exploration. Test constraints and responsiveness across device sizes. No one-click build; developers still essential for production. AI sentiment: hybrid-operator stance—AI for creative generation and assembly, humans for strategy and final polish. Figma isn't disappearing but is no longer the design bottleneck; it's now a collaboration/polish layer.

operating_rules: AI is a workflow, not a tool—requires multi-tool orchestration, not single-tool mastery
Design systems must be trained sequentially: variables first, styles second, components third, in logical groupings
Always provide visual reference (screenshots, Mobbin examples) to AI; don't rely on text descriptions alone
Use constraints + auto layout for responsive; manual pixel pushing doesn't scale
Components are leverage: edit once, propagate everywhere; use for navigation, buttons, cards, any reusable element
Test on real devices and simulators; Figma canvas ≠ production reality
Token efficiency: fast exploration (Stitch), iterative polish (Codeex), high-fidelity/production (Claude)
Figma MCP is read-write: push designs from code, pull context into code; bidirectional workflow
Hand off includes training: Notion portal with CMS videos, README in file structure, layer naming conventions
Design for emotion first; audit every decision against a single core emotional intent, not aesthetics

content_ideas: Deep dive: token accounting across Claude/Codeex workflows—show real per-project costs
Figma MCP advanced patterns: bi-directional sync for design → dev → design loops
Design system training masterclass: how to structure variables, styles, components so AI learns them correctly
iOS app blueprint: Figma → Windsurf → TestFlight in <2 hours (prerequisite: solid wireframes)
Pre-mortem design thinking: test logo in motion, text at tiny sizes, colors on edge cases before handoff
Emotion-driven design: framework for defining one core feeling, then auditing every pixel against it
File structure as professionalism: naming layers, README folders, export instructions that make handoff seamless
Responsive design without guessing: constraints + auto layout + multiple viewport testing checklist
contradictions: Figma is essential for design but NOT the bottleneck anymore (AI can generate designs faster than hand-crafting); tension between tools and human intent
Claude Design produces highest quality but is token-expensive; Codeex is token-efficient but lower quality—no single right choice
Design systems should be built manually (for deep understanding) but AI can generate them fast (saves time but less intentional)
Prototyping in Figma is powerful but AI can prototype code faster; Figma is now a polish/collaboration layer, not the source of truth
Responsive design via constraints + auto layout is systematic but testing across real devices reveals edge cases constraints miss
weird_gold: Google Stitch produces consistently worse designs than Claude but is perfect for very fast, token-free early-stage exploration when stakeholders are indecisive—'validate before you build'
Swap fill and stroke with Shift+X in Figma; tiny shortcut with huge workflow impact
Designing websites like designing homes (rooms = pages, spaces = sections) is a conceptual frame that made the whole architecture coherent
Mobbin (competitor research app) + AI is the inverse of pure AI: visual references beat 1000-word prompts every time
iOS apps can be shipped in <1 hour with Figma → Windsurf → TestFlight IF you plan wireframes first (proof: mood tracker built in ~50 min live on camera)
Industrial designers bring craft (clicking sounds, manufacturing intent) that software designers often miss; AI lacks this intentionality layer
Zapier + multi-stage form = lead qualification automation; saved the architecture firm 10 hours/week manually screening inquiries
notes: Document is a 10-segment video transcript (YouTube/educational content) covering the full AI design workflow as of 2024-2025. Heavy emphasis on practical workflow orchestration, not just tool features. Includes 3 major sections: AI tools comparison (Claude/Codeex/Stitch/Claude Design), design system training for AI, and end-to-end case studies (web design for architecture firm, iOS mood tracker app). Critical insight: AI is not a replacement for designers; it's a force multiplier when used in structured workflows. Token efficiency and bidirectional Figma MCP are game-changers. No content on 3D design, motion graphics depth, or enterprise-scale design systems. Assumes intermediate+ designer audience. Some mentions of paid tools (Mobbin, Brilliant, UI Collective Academy) but not promotional. Production quality high; pacing and examples clear.
